reason: Conversation 1 immediately gave the correct safety instruction (switch off at the consumer unit, don't touch wet plugs/extension lead), got the homeowner to actually isolate the power, and then correctly and confidently identified the Fairy washing-up liquid as the cause with no unsupported part claims; its only weakness is slight overreach in insisting on an engineer before any further use rather than steering toward an electrician check of the wet socket/lead plus rinse cycles. Conversation 2 opened with generic leak causes (filter, spray arm) before gathering facts, then got stuck in a loop when the homeowner couldn't find the fuse box, ending with the machine still running and water nearly at the extension lead, while making the dubious claim that the 0800 40 50 60 power-cut line could 'isolate the power at their end' for a single property. It also never moved the homeowner to a resolved, safe state or committed to the clear detergent diagnosis, so Conversation 1 served the homeowner clearly better on both safety outcome and diagnosis.
